zh.label: 片刻随记 · 07
zh.title: AI 做首页做得很漂亮，为什么别人还是看不懂？
zh.excerpt: 首页可以有气质，也要讲清楚：这是什么，和读者有什么关系，点击以后能做什么。
zh.content:
![PRODUCT NOTES 02 · 让价值更清楚](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/cover.png)

你花了很久让 AI 选字体、调配色，让 AI 换了几版布局，终于把首页做得像样了。

把链接发出去，对方看完却问：“所以，你这个到底是做什么的？”

这句话有点让人泄气。明明首页上写了那么多，怎么还没讲清楚？

我会先回头看看首屏的文字。我们很容易把自己的愿望写上去，却忘了告诉第一次来的人：

这里有什么，和你有什么关系，你可以先做什么。

## 01 / PRODUCT NOTES｜一句动听的话，未必是一句有用的介绍

“重新连接自己”“探索无限可能”“开启全新体验”。

这些话放在页面上，通常不难看。但遮住产品名，你能判断它介绍的是冥想 App、旅行网站，还是一门课程吗？

如果换成另一个产品也完全说得通，这句话可能还没有把你真正做的东西说出来。

这不意味着品牌不能有诗意。只是第一次见面时，读者需要一点具体的东西，才能知道是否值得继续看。

先让人理解，情绪才有落脚的地方。

## 02 / PRODUCT NOTES｜拿一休来说，我会怎样介绍它？

一休是我做的冥想与自然声产品。你可以在声音库中选声音，再到播放页调整音量与聆听时长。

下面是它的真实 App 截图：自然声播放页和三分钟呼吸练习页。

![01 / 聆听自然声 · 一休 App 实机截图](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/player.png)

![02 / 三分钟呼吸 · 一休 App 实机截图](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/breathing.png)

如果要为它写一个面向睡前聆听场景的首页，我会先做这样一组文案练习。

第一种写法：“开启你的宁静之旅。用科技与美学，重新连接自己。”按钮是“立即探索”。

第二种写法：“睡前，听一段让你安静下来的自然声。雨声、海浪、鸟鸣。选一种声音，设置时长，开始聆听。”按钮是“试听自然声”。

第二种说法给了读者更多判断的依据：什么时候用，有什么内容，进去以后能做什么。

![以一休为例的首页文案练习 · 非线上页面或效果测试](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/copy-comparison.png)

这组对照是表达练习，不是一休线上首页的改版，也没有转化数据。它说明的是信息变得具体了；是否更适合目标读者，还需要实际观察。

还有一个取舍：写“睡前”，就会弱化专注、阅读等场景。如果这一页主要服务睡前用户，这是有意的聚焦；如果它是介绍全部功能的官网首页，就需要更宽的表达。

清楚，也包括知道这一页优先对谁说话。

## 03 / PRODUCT NOTES｜先回答三个问题，再调整页面

我会先把首屏要讲的内容，写成三句普通话。

### 这是给谁、在什么时候用的？

让读者认出自己的处境。例如“睡前脑子还很忙”，就比一个宽泛的人群标签更接近日常。

### 这里具体有什么，能帮他做什么？

把“全新体验”换成能看见、能理解的内容。声音、模板、一份报告、一项操作，都可以成为具体的入口。

### 点下按钮以后，会发生什么？

“试听自然声”“查看示例报告”“创建第一个页面”，让人能预期下一步。如果按钮写着试听，点击后却先要求填写一长串信息，这份清楚就断在了行动上。

这三件事确定以后，再用字号、留白和图片安排阅读顺序。视觉的作用，是让重要的信息更容易被看见。

## 04 / PRODUCT NOTES｜把 AI 当成第一次来到首页的人

你可以把首页截图和文字交给 AI，先做一轮检查：

> 请只根据这张首页判断：这是什么产品，适合谁，能完成什么，点击主按钮后会发生什么？每个判断都指出页面上的依据。无法判断的地方，直接说不知道，不要替我补充。

> 然后指出最值得先改的一句话，给我三个更具体的版本。不要增加原产品没有的功能或效果承诺。

它的回答可以帮助发现表达上的空缺，但不能代替真实读者。

再找一个不了解产品的人，看完以后，用自己的话说说“这是做什么的”。先听他的理解，别急着解释。那些需要你在旁边补充的话，往往就是页面还没讲清楚的地方。

今天如果只改一件事，就试着把首页那句最动听、也最模糊的话，改得更具体一点。

好的首页，可以有气质，也应该让人知道自己为什么要留下来。

你现在的首页第一句话是什么？把产品名遮住以后，它还能让人认出你在做什么吗？

Elian · Design × AI × Product

把想法做成真正的产品。

en.label: FIELD NOTES · 07
en.title: AI Made Your Homepage Beautiful. Why Do People Still Not Understand It?
en.excerpt: A homepage can have character and still be clear: what is here, why it matters to the reader, and what happens after they click.
en.content:
![PRODUCT NOTES 02 · Making the Value Clearer — original Chinese cover](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/cover.png)

You spent a long time asking AI to choose fonts, adjust colors, and try several layouts. Finally, the homepage looks presentable.

You send someone the link. After looking at it, they ask, “So what does this actually do?”

That can be discouraging. There is so much writing on the homepage. How can the message still be unclear?

I would start by looking again at the words on the first screen. It is easy to put our own aspirations there and forget to tell a first-time visitor: what is here, why it matters to them, and what they can do first.

## 01 / PRODUCT NOTES｜A Beautiful Phrase Is Not Always a Useful Introduction

“Reconnect with yourself.” “Explore infinite possibilities.” “Begin a whole new experience.”

These phrases rarely look out of place on a page. But cover up the product name: can you tell whether they describe a meditation app, a travel website, or a course?

If the same sentence works perfectly well for another product, it may not yet explain what you actually make.

That does not mean a brand cannot be poetic. It means that, at a first meeting, readers need something concrete to decide whether to keep reading.

Help people understand first. Then the emotion has somewhere to land.

## 02 / PRODUCT NOTES｜How Would I Introduce Yixiu?

Yixiu is the meditation and nature-sound product I built. You can choose a sound in its library, then adjust the volume and listening duration on the player screen.

Below are real app screenshots: the nature-sound player and a three-minute breathing practice.

![01 / Listen to nature sounds — actual Yixiu app screenshot](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/player.png)

![02 / Three-minute breathing practice — actual Yixiu app screenshot](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/breathing.png)

If I were writing a homepage specifically for listening before bed, I would begin with this copy exercise.

The first version: “Begin your journey to tranquility. Reconnect with yourself through technology and aesthetics.” The button says “Explore now.”

The second version: “Before bed, listen to nature sounds that help you settle down. Rain, waves, birdsong. Choose a sound, set the duration, and start listening.” The button says “Preview nature sounds.”

The second version gives readers more to judge by: when to use it, what content is available, and what they can do once they enter.

![A homepage-copy exercise using Yixiu: abstract language versus concrete information. This is not a live-page redesign or a performance test. Original Chinese illustration.](/assets/notes/2026-09-15-ai-homepage-clarity/copy-comparison.png)

This comparison is an exercise in expression, not a redesign of Yixiu's live homepage, and there are no conversion data. It shows that the information has become more specific. Whether it better suits the intended readers still needs to be observed in practice.

There is also a trade-off: saying “before bed” gives less attention to other situations, such as focus or reading. If the page primarily serves bedtime listeners, that is an intentional focus. If it is the main website homepage introducing every feature, the wording needs to be broader.

Clarity also means knowing whom this particular page is speaking to first.

## 03 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Answer Three Questions Before Adjusting the Page

I would first write the message of the opening screen as three plain statements.

### Who Is This For, and When Would They Use It?

Let readers recognize their own situation. “Your mind is still busy before bed,” for example, is closer to everyday experience than a broad audience label.

### What Exactly Is Here, and What Can It Help Them Do?

Replace “a whole new experience” with content people can see and understand. A sound, a template, a report, or an action can all provide a concrete starting point.

### What Happens After They Press the Button?

“Preview nature sounds,” “View a sample report,” and “Create your first page” let people anticipate the next step. If a button promises a preview but first asks them to fill in a long form, the clarity breaks down at the point of action.

Once these three things are settled, use type size, whitespace, and imagery to organize the reading sequence. The role of visual design is to make the important information easier to notice.

## 04 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Ask AI to Look Like a First-Time Visitor

You can give AI a screenshot and the homepage text for an initial check:

> Based only on this homepage, what is the product, who is it for, what can someone accomplish with it, and what happens after they press the main button? For every judgment, point to the evidence on the page. When you cannot tell, say that you do not know. Do not fill in the gaps for me.
> Then identify the one sentence most worth changing first and give me three more specific versions. Do not add features or promises of results that the original product does not offer.

Its response may help you find gaps in the message, but it cannot replace real readers.

Find someone unfamiliar with the product and, after they look at the page, ask them to explain in their own words what it does. Listen to their understanding before rushing to explain. The things you need to add in person are often exactly what the page has not made clear.

If you change just one thing today, try making the homepage's most beautiful—and most vague—sentence a little more specific.

A good homepage can have character. It should also help people understand why they might want to stay.

What is the first sentence on your homepage right now? If you cover up the product name, can people still recognize what you do?

Elian · Design × AI × Product

Turning ideas into real products.
